# The integral image of signed restriction to a spanning circuit

## Abstract

Exact integral restriction image for arbitrary spanning circuits.

**Theorem 1.1 (The image is generated by the dual parallel-class sizes).**

$$\forall (V: \operatorname{Type}_{u}) [\operatorname{LinearOrder}\left(V\right)] [\operatorname{Fintype}\left(V\right)] (M: \operatorname{Matroid}\left(V\right)) (K: \operatorname{Finset}\left(V\right)), \operatorname{IsCircuit}\left(M, (K: \operatorname{Set}\left(V\right))\right) \Rightarrow \operatorname{Spanning}\left(M, (K: \operatorname{Set}\left(V\right))\right) \Rightarrow \forall (n: \mathbb{Z}), ((\exists (z: \operatorname{Chain}\left(V\right)), \operatorname{TopCycle}\left(M, z\right) \land \operatorname{signedRestriction}\left(K, z\right) = n) \Leftrightarrow ((\operatorname{dualClassGcd}\left(M, K\right): \mathbb{Z}) \mid n))$$

*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Matroids/SpanningCircuitImage.exists_topCycle_signedRestriction_iff` (`✓ std3`). ∎

*Source.* Repository-derived.

*Commentary.*

Let M be a matroid on a finite linearly ordered carrier, and let K be a spanning circuit in M. A top augmented integral cycle is a function on finite faces that vanishes off the bases and has zero augmented boundary. Its signed restriction is the sum of its coefficients on the single-vertex deletions of K, weighted by the corresponding boundary signs. The attainable integers are exactly the multiples of the gcd of the sizes of the fibers in K of the dual singleton-closure map.

Write E for the matroid ground. Each deletion of a vertex a of K is a primal base because K is a spanning circuit. Its complement in E is the dual base consisting of a and all vertices in E outside K. Together these bases show that every ground vertex is a dual nonloop. If distinct a and b in K have the same dual singleton closure, they form a dual circuit. In the primal boundary at K with a and b deleted, every insertion except a and b has zero coefficient. A vertex outside E cannot give a base. Every insertion from E outside K leaves the dual circuit in the complement. The two remaining boundary terms equate the signed restriction coordinates at a and b, with the relative sign fixed by the identity that the simplex boundary has zero boundary.

For the converse, choose a representative p of a dual parallel class in K and start with the dual base consisting of p and E outside K. First contract the closure of p. Every singleton in that flat is a basis of the flat. The chosen base loses only p, and the contraction is again loopless on its ground. Repeat with a vertex of the residual base until the ground is empty, where the chain is the empty simplex. The signed join of the augmented simplex boundaries on the successive removed flats has zero boundary by the Leibniz rule. Every nonzero coefficient omits exactly one element from each flat. The basis rule for contraction makes the omitted set a dual base, so the coefficient is on a primal base.

At the deletion of p the join has a unit coefficient. At a deletion outside the first flat, that face retains the whole first flat and its coefficient vanishes. The first flat is contained in K, since the dual base contains every ground vertex outside K. Multiplying by the signed coordinate at p gives signed coordinate one throughout its class and zero elsewhere. These cycles realize the individual class sizes. Grouping the signed coordinates of any cycle by class gives divisibility by their gcd, and finite integer Bezout yields a linear combination of the class cycles for every multiple.

The ground can be proper in the carrier, and K can equal the ground. The augmented boundary convention includes the empty face for a singleton circuit. The statement uses the integral readout directly, including the rank-zero contraction coordinate.
